purpose: This is a number line where absolute value means distance. You move a test point and watch its distance from a fixed point, so |x - a| = k and |x - a| < k turn into questions about how far away you are.

stops.title: The number line
stops.text: The violet dot is the fixed number a. The ring with a blue centre is your test point x. The blue bar is the distance between them, and its label says how long it is. The label turns green or red.
stops.try: Drag the ring left and right and watch the blue bar grow and shrink.

stops.title: Test point
stops.text: This slider moves the same ring as dragging does, one step at a time. The readout under it works out the distance and tests it against the statement: Yes means x is a solution.
stops.try: Find a number where the readout says Yes, then look for a second one.

stops.title: Build the graph
stops.text: In the Within and beyond step you draw the answer yourself. Pick between or outside, open or closed circles, and set the two edges with the - and + buttons or by dragging the two small circles.
stops.try: Press Check my graph. A wrong graph gets a hint, not a penalty.

stops.title: Open or closed
stops.text: An open circle means that exact number is not a solution. A closed circle means it is. Strict signs (< and >) use open circles. Signs with 'or equal' use closed ones.
stops.try: Switch the sign at the top to at most, then see which circles Check my graph wants.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 asks you to predict, then mark both solutions of |x-2|=3. Step 2 is graphing inequalities. Step 3 solves an equation with a line inside the bars. Step 4 has stories and no-answer cases.

stops.title: Try practice problems
stops.text: Seven short problems on the same number line: equations, graphs, a tricky one and a lost-solution puzzle. Nothing is scored or saved.
stops.try: Start practice and aim to solve the first one without a hint.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Three questions to finish. A wrong answer shows why, and you can try again.

teacher: Project step 1 and ask: how many numbers are 3 away from 2? Students often find only 5 and forget -1, which is the lost-solution mistake. In step 2, ask them to test the centre point before choosing between or outside.
